authors: Caimi, Langlais, Fontana, Wunnava, Bellini, Braun, Fraccia
claim: 2',3'-cyclic nucleotides of all four bases polymerise without added activators under room-temperature wet-dry cycling at mildly alkaline pH; yield ~70% for G and >=20% for others; at pH 11 balanced polymerisation, Y=36%; up to 6% 4-mers and 0.1% 10-mers.
note: Short oligomers only; growth and hydrolysis balance after ~10 cycles. Full text: Room temperature = 23 C, pH set with KOH (9-12; optimum 10-11), up to 10 daily cycles, 2 replicates; methods cannot distinguish 2'-5' from 3'-5' linkages (likely ~1:1); hydrolysis limits length at high pH; cyclic nucleotides were purchased, not made prebiotically.

claim: In water from one Icelandic hot spring (Seltun), 16 wet-dry cycles degraded 95% of AMP and 63% of UMP, and 4 cycles destroyed ~90% of A10 and U10; in water from another (Hveradalir) nucleotides were as stable as in nuclease-free water.
note: Natural water chemistry can make or break the pond scenario. Full text not read: Closed access (OpenAlex oa=closed); not in Europe PMC or PMC.

claim: Proposes template-directed replication and chiral resolution during wet-dry cycling in hydrothermal pools.
note: Hypothesis/review-type paper; claim limited to its title. Full text: A Perspective backed only by kinetic simulations (Kintecus, 25 C) of racemic, unactivated RNA monomers; no new experiments; equal homo-D/homo-L output is a modelling artefact the authors note.

claim: Heat flow through thin rock cracks separates >50 prebiotic building blocks from mixtures; in modelled crack networks concentration ratios rise up to 1000-fold, and purifying trimetaphosphate raises glycine dimerisation yield by up to five orders of magnitude (experiments in single and three-chamber set-ups showed smaller gains).
note: Physical process that could replace purified hand-offs; relevant to the compatibility rule. Full text: The up-to-1000-fold ratios and the five-orders-of-magnitude yield gain come from numerical models of large crack networks (20x20 chambers) built on measured Soret coefficients; experiments used one chamber or a three-chamber network (e.g. 23-fold N/I enrichment), and the modelled yield reaches ~10% at dT = 10 K.

authors: Ianeselli, Atienza, Kudella, Gerland, Mast, Braun
claim: Water cycles in a Hadean CO2 atmosphere drive the evolution of long DNA.
note: Pre-2023 context; details not checked. Full text: Replication was done by Taq DNA polymerase ('to mimic a sped-up RNA world'), not non-enzymatically; dew from 0.1-1 bar CO2 at pH ~4 melted strands 30 K below bulk Tm; >1,000-nt AT-rich strands emerged.

claim: Experimental and computational study of peptide bond formation driven by wet-dry cycles and gamma radiation.
note: Details not checked. Full text: One amino acid only (solid DL-glutamic acid, 40 kGy gamma dose); peptide bond evidence is a dimer at m/z 275 by MS plus IR/DSC/TGA shifts, with HyperChem modelling; the authors call the results preliminary.

claim: Lipid bilayer vesicles form de novo, without pre-existing membranes, from acetate and cysteine; lipid tails are built by soluble enzymes; glycolipid compartments hold proton gradients.
note: Uses enzymes, so it addresses membrane heredity, not a prebiotic route. Full text: Soluble enzymes are modern purified ones (E. coli ACS, human ACC, C. glutamicum FAS) fed ATP, CoA, NADPH, HCO3-; headgroup attached non-enzymatically by native chemical ligation; the glycolipid used a synthetic galactosaminothiol headgroup; it lost 19 +/- 7% of the pH gradient over 12 h vs 83% for the cysteine lipid.

authors: Baba, Yokoyama, Sato, Asanuma et al.
claim: Defined peptide sequences change the growth rate of fatty-acid vesicles; the sequence-growth relationship forms a fitness landscape with epistasis.
note: Sequence information coupled to compartment growth; no heredity of composition shown. Full text: Small landscape: 10 dipeptides from four amino acids (Leu, Gly, Glu, His) plus Leu/Gly tripeptides, in decanoic acid vesicles; growth measured over 2 h by DLS and cryo-TEM.

authors: Cohen, Todd, Maibaum, Catling et al.
claim: Stabilisation of prebiotic vesicles by peptides depends on sequence and chirality.
note: Details not checked. Full text: Read the 2023 preprint, not the published version. Chirality effect is destabilising: heterochiral Leu-Leu (L-D or D-L) shrinks decanoic-acid vesicles and makes them leakier, homochiral does not; 3 of 15 dipeptides (all with leucine) reduce salt-induced flocculation.

claim: Non-enzymatic oligonucleotide ligation in coacervate protocells sustains compartment-content coupling.
note: Coacervates, not lipid vesicles; details not checked. Full text: DNA (Drew-Dickerson dodecamer) ligated with carbodiimide activation in coacervates made with a synthetic azobenzene photoswitch; not a prebiotic chemistry, and the genotype-phenotype link is proposed, not shown across sequences.

claim: Argues for an evolutionary path from compositional assemblies (composomes, the lipid-world GARD model) to an RNA replicase.
note: Theory paper by lipid-world proponents; details not checked. Full text: Purely theoretical ('No new data were created or analyzed'); the replicase is proposed to arise by self-assembly of short RNAs (stable complex evolution) rather than selection, and spreads by reassembly, not self-copying; authors concede it may not be falsifiable.

claim: Model of lipid vesicle growth and division driven by an autocatalytic reaction.
note: Computational. Full text: Purely computational; division needs slow lipid flip-flop between leaflets, gives unequal daughters, and only vesicles with an active internal autocatalytic reaction reach a steady growth-division cycle.

authors: Gianni, Kwok, Wan, Goeij, Clifton, Colizzi, Attwater, Holliger
claim: QT45, a 45-nt polymerase ribozyme from random pools, copies RNA from triplet substrates in mildly alkaline eutectic ice; made its complementary strand (94.1% per-nt fidelity, random triplets) and itself (defined triplets), each at ~0.2% yield in 72 days.
note: Plan's second-hand '0.02% over 72 days' is wrong: the abstract gives ~0.2% yield. Online 2026-02-12. Full text: Both strands made in separate, primer-extension reactions (not a closed self-replication cycle); the self (+) copy needed one defined hexamer besides triplets; conditions pH 9, -7 C frozen, ribozyme in 10-fold excess; yields 0.24% (-) and 0.17% (+).

authors: Attwater, Augustin, Curran, Kwok, Ohlendorf, Gianni, Holliger
claim: Triplet substrates trap separated strands; with coupled pH and freeze-thaw cycles a polymerase ribozyme replicates both strands of dsRNAs exponentially, including a fragment of the ribozyme itself; open-ended runs from random pools gave replicating sequences or drifting diverse pools.
note: Contradicts site text 'no exponential growth yet' for RNA world. Not whole-ribozyme self-replication, not scenario feedstocks. Full text: Amplification is modest and short-lived (e.g. 9- and 31-fold overall for a defined duplex; 1.2-1.38-fold per cycle for ~4 cycles before plateau); the ribozyme itself is supplied, and only a fragment of it is replicated.

claim: A higher-fidelity polymerase ribozyme propagates a hammerhead ribozyme through rounds of replication and selection; the high-fidelity lineage evolved fitter variants, the low-fidelity lineage lost function.
note: Plan verified citation only; details now checked. Full text: Fidelity 89.1% (71-89) vs 81.4% (52-2) for reciprocal synthesis of a modified hammerhead (27 nt copied, primers supply the rest); 8 rounds per lineage with reverse transcription, PCR and transcription by protein enzymes between rounds; the polymerase itself did not evolve.

authors: McRae, Wan, Kristoffersen et al. (Holliger, Andersen)
claim: 5-A cryo-EM structure of a triplet polymerase ribozyme: a heterodimer of catalytic and auxiliary subunits joined by two kissing loops, plus a mutational functional map.
note: Full text: Structure is of the apoenzyme only (template bound too transiently to resolve), with local resolution 5-9 A; the holoenzyme mechanism is a model.

claim: Review of emergent and convergent features in laboratory evolution of polymerase ribozymes.
note: Full text not read: Closed access (OpenAlex oa=closed); no open copy.

claim: Nonenzymatic RNA copying with a potentially primordial genetic alphabet.
note: Details not checked. Full text: Alphabet is A, I, s2U, s2C: A:s2U and I:s2C pairs are isoenergetic and isomorphic; shown by thermodynamics, crystal structures and primer-extension kinetics, but a purine-vs-pyrimidine dinucleotide binding bias remains and full copying of mixed sequences is not shown.

authors: Duzdevich, Carr, Colville, Aitken et al.
claim: Overcoming nucleotide bias in nonenzymatic copying of RNA templates.
note: Details not checked. Full text: Bias (strong G/C preference) reduced by adding a random-sequence oligonucleotide mix (2-16 nt) to activated mononucleotides with methyl isocyanide activation; still cannot copy ribozyme-length templates; error rate ~6%.

authors: Pressman, Liu, Janzen, Blanco et al.
claim: Systematic fitness landscape of self-aminoacylating ribozymes.
note: Plan's year and journal correct; DOI found here. Full text: Near-complete coverage of a central 21-nt region only; three ribozyme families separated by low-activity valleys, so the landscape is frustrated and global optimisation is blocked.

claim: High-throughput mutational analysis of a twister ribozyme.
note: Plan's memory citation confirmed. Full text: All 10,296 single and double mutants of the 54-nt Osa-1-4 twister ribozyme assayed by deep sequencing of co-transcriptional self-cleavage; highly robust (71% of single, 30% of double mutants keep >20% relative activity); semiquantitative, single 2 h time point.

authors: Hudson, de Graaf, Strandoo Rodin, ... Braun, Sojo
claim: H2 reduces CO2 to formate at room temperature and 1.5 bar, driven by microfluidic pH gradients across Fe(Ni)S precipitates; reducing the gradient, removing H2 or the precipitate gave no detectable product.
note: Correct. Full text: Yields are tiny (average ~1.5 uM formate) and need a steep gradient (acidic ocean side pH 3.9 vs alkaline vent side up to pH ~12.6); deuterium labelling points to an electrochemical mechanism, not direct hydrogenation.

claim: Macroscale vent-ocean reactor: FeS, Ni-FeS and FeS2 barriers give micromolar formic and acetic acid on the ocean side under pH gradients (e.g. 4.2 uM formic, 2.5 uM acetic with FeS2 at 25 C); currents of 10 nA-10 uA suffice.
note: Correct. Note 75 C runs reached ~816 uM formic acid.

authors: Nan, Luo, Tran, Fahrenbach, ... Van Kranendonk
claim: FeS (pure or doped) catalyses H2-driven CO2 reduction to methanol under simulated hot-spring vapour conditions; Mn doping raises methanol five-fold at 120 C.
note: Terrestrial hot-spring analogue, not a vent. Author correction 10.1038/s41467-024-55040-0. Full text: Gas-phase flow reactor at 80-120 C and ambient pressure, FeS on SiO2 doped with Ti, Ni, Mn or Co (10%); rates in umol/g/min; authors flag uncertainty over how persistent H2, CO2, heat and light were. Article has a later correction (Nat Commun 15:10644).

claim: Activated pyrimidine ribonucleotides form via arabinose amino-oxazoline and anhydronucleoside intermediates, bypassing free ribose and nucleobases; phosphate present from the start controls earlier steps.
note: Landmark. Full text not read: Closed access (OpenAlex oa=closed); not in Europe PMC or PMC.

claim: Common origins of RNA, protein and lipid precursors in a cyanosulfidic protometabolism.
note: Full text: Precursors of pyrimidine ribonucleotides, 12 amino acids and glycerol phosphate come from HCN reductive homologation with H2S, UV and Cu(I)/Cu(II); not one pot - reagents need sequential delivery, proposed via streams and pools.

claim: Thiophosphate photochemistry gives prebiotic access to sugars and terpenoid precursors.
note: Details not checked. Full text: UV/HCN photochemistry; tetroses and pentoses form without running on to higher sugars; the terpenoid precursors are the C5 alcohols (dimethylallyl and isopentenyl alcohol), not the phosphorylated IPP/DMAPP.

claim: Forward-synthesis algorithm generates a network of prebiotic reactions from primordial substrates; finds new routes, catalytic emergence and a self-regenerating cycle of iminodiacetic acid, partly validated by experiment.
note: Citation real. The plan's use of it as evidence that cyanosulfidic chemistry 'needs ordered delivery' is not what the abstract says. Full text not read: Closed access (OpenAlex oa=closed); no open copy.

authors: Singh, Thoma, Whitaker, Satterly Webley, Yao, Powner
claim: Aminoacyl-thiols react selectively with RNA 2',3'-diols over amines, favouring aminoacylation over uncoded peptide bonds; prebiotic nitriles, NCAs and anhydrides give aminoacyl-thiols in water; one-pot peptidyl-RNA at neutral pH.
note: Title in news.json was paraphrased; real title used now. Full text: Peptidyl-RNA is a two-step, one-pot sequence: the peptide bond step needs a switch from thioester to thioacid activation, which inverts the diol/amine selectivity.

claim: Adding all cofactors relevant to the anaerobic network to the food set gives a maxRAF of 1335 reactions, 25% of the network; inorganic food alone gives 8 reactions.
note: Correct.

claim: Remnants of an ancient metabolism without phosphate (network expansion).
note: Real; details not checked. Full text not read: Listed as hybrid OA but cell.com PDF/full text and ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; no PMC copy.

authors: Sharma, Czegel, Lachmann, Kempes, Walker, Cronin
claim: Introduces assembly (A) as a measure of the causation needed to produce an ensemble of objects, as a quantification of selection.
note: Full text: Theoretical framework; assembly (A) combines each object's assembly index with its copy number, and the framework is contested (see Hazen et al., Abrahao et al.).

authors: Marshall, Mathis, Carrick, Keenan et al. (Cronin)
claim: Identifying molecules as biosignatures with assembly theory and mass spectrometry.
note: Real; data source for task #7. Full text: Only living samples gave MA above ~15 (threshold set from a small sample set measured by Orbitrap MS/MS); some biological samples (bay sediment, whisky) fell below it, and high MA marks living or technological processes, not life alone.

authors: Hazen, Burns, Cleaves, Downs, Krivovichev, Wong
claim: Mineral heteropolyanions have assembly indices from 2 up to 21 (ewingite, ilmajokite), so indices >=15 are not unambiguous biosignatures.
note: Correct. Full text: Indices depend on the counting method (e.g. ewingite 18 or 20, ilmajokite 18 or 21; ewingite could be as low as 16 if its disordered carbonates are arranged differently); all still >=15. Some of the most complex minerals form by oxidation that may owe something to biology, though others are purely igneous/metamorphic.

claim: Reply: their ~15 threshold is from experimentally measured covalent organic molecules; Hazen's indices are theoretical, from crystal structures of charged units not isolable in solution.
note: Plan gave no venue; now identified. Full text: Authors concede the threshold 'might shift with more experimental data' and need not be the same for minerals; in the main text they say heteropolyanions can be isolated in solution but are very labile.

authors: Hazen, Burns, Cleaves, Downs et al.
claim: Counter-reply to Walker et al.
note: Full text: The reply concedes ground: values are calculated minimum assembly pathways, not measured indices; abiotic heteropolyanions appear capped below ~25, which the authors say supports AT's core idea if the threshold is raised and if it applies to inorganic molecules at all.

claim: The assembly pathway method is an encoding scheme used by statistical compression algorithms and performs like simple coding schemes.
note: The plan put this author list on the PLOS Complex Systems paper; that paper is by Abrahao et al. Full text: Argument rests on correlations (e.g. MA vs LZW R=0.87 on 99 molecules; MA vs RLE R=0.9 on 18 extracts) using Marshall et al. 2021 data they could not fully reproduce; they also claim coding indexes outperform MA at separating living from non-living.

claim: Claims assembly index equals the size of a minimal context-free grammar, with compressibility bounded by Shannon entropy and LZ schemes.
note: Plan wrote 'Uthamacumaran, Abrahao & Zenil 2024 (PLOS Complex Systems)'; corrected. Full text: The paper's stronger conclusion is that assembly index and assembly number explain or quantify nothing about selection that Shannon entropy or algorithmic complexity could not; proofs are in the S1 Appendix, and the equivalence is disputed by the AT authors.

authors: Kempes, Lachmann, Iannaccone, Fricke et al.
claim: Argues assembly index is distinct from Shannon entropy, Huffman and LZW, and belongs to a different computational complexity class.
note: Correct. Full text: Class argument is that assembly index is NP-complete while LZ/Huffman/Shannon run in polynomial time, so it holds only if P != NP; proofs are for strings, and they do not rule out equivalence to some NP-complete compression scheme.

authors: Ozelim, Uthamacumaran, Abrahao, Hernandez-Orozco et al.
claim: Reply: the 2025 defence's experiments are incomplete as controls; extended, they overlap with dictionary-based compression.
note: Published 2026-07-04; volume/pages not yet in Crossref. Full text not read: Publisher page shows only the abstract (no body sections); the .pdf link redirects back to the abstract page and the listed _reference.pdf is the reference list. Only the supplementary PDF (from p. 45) was available. The claim matches the abstract.

claim: Assembly theory: what it does and what it does not do.
note: Commentary. Full text: Essay: assembly theory detects and quantifies bias from higher-level constraints but cannot say whether that bias is due to natural selection, ignores function, and is 'not nearly as novel or revolutionary as claimed'.

claim: Racemic ribo-aminooxazoline crystallised on magnetite: direct crystallisation not consistently selective; recrystallisation gives ~60% ee at best and ~35% ee on average; above ~25% ee a further crystallisation gives homochiral crystals.
note: Plan correct; site text gave only the 35% average.

claim: Model: homochirality emerges via template-directed ligation in an RNA reactor.
note: Computational. Full text: Stochastic simulations only; template-free polymerisation cannot reach high homochirality, and full homochirality needs non-equilibrium driving (e.g. temperature cycling) plus kinetic stalling of ligation after chiral mismatches. Read the arXiv v2 (Apr 2024) because APS returned 403.

authors: Glavin, Dworkin, Alexander, Aponte et al. (62 authors)
claim: Bennu: 33 amino acids (14 of the 20 protein ones), all five nucleobases, ~10,000 N-bearing species, abundant ammonia; chiral non-protein amino acids racemic or near racemic.
note: News text said 'the amino acids are racemic' and 'uncontaminated'; paper says chiral non-protein amino acids racemic, plus racemic Ala and Asp, and samples pristine.

authors: Furukawa, Sunami, Takano, Koga et al.
claim: Bennu: ribose 0.097 +/- 0.014 nmol/g, glucose 0.35 +/- 0.05 nmol/g, plus lyxose, xylose, arabinose, galactose; 2-deoxyribose not found.
note: Online 2025-12-02, issue Jan 2026.

claim: Bennu samples hold sodium phosphates, carbonates, sulfates, chlorides and fluorides from evaporation of a late-stage brine.
note: Full text: Salts are micron-scale veins and grains (trace phases); they decay in air (halite/sylvite gone after 8 months), so they survived only in nitrogen-stored samples; trona, sulfate and fluoride identifications are tentative.

authors: Koga, Oba, Takano, Naraoka et al.
claim: All five canonical nucleobases in Ryugu; near-equal purines and pyrimidines; purine/pyrimidine ratio falls with ammonia across Ryugu, Bennu and Orgueil.
note: Full text: The ammonia trend is a correlation (R2 = 0.89) across four samples (two Ryugu, Bennu, Orgueil), with ammonia measured in other aggregate samples; the ammonia effect has not been tested experimentally. Murchison is purine-rich and Bennu/Orgueil pyrimidine-rich; nucleobases are at pmol/g levels.

authors: Naraoka, Takano, Dworkin, Oba et al.
claim: Soluble organic molecules in Ryugu samples.
note: Details not checked. Full text not read: Green OA copy at hal.science is behind an anti-bot (Anubis) gate that refused automated access; publisher copy closed; not in Europe PMC.

claim: Uracil in Ryugu.
note: Full text: Uracil found in aqueous extracts of two Ryugu samples (A0106, C0107) at different concentrations; nicotinic acid and imidazoles were also detected; only uracil among nucleobases in this study.

claim: Electric discharge through CH4, NH3, H2O and H2 produced amino acids.
checked_against: Crossref/PubMed record; full text not opened (paywall)
note: Landmark; no yields quoted. Full text not read: Closed access (OpenAlex oa=closed); no open copy.

claim: LUCA ~4.2 Ga (4.09-4.33); genome >=2.5 Mb, ~2,600 proteins; prokaryote-grade anaerobic acetogen with an early immune system, part of an ecosystem.
note: Correct. Full text: Point estimates are 2.75 Mb (2.49-2.99) and 2,657 proteins (2,451-2,855), from integrating gene-presence probabilities, many of them low; the age rests on five pre-LUCA paralogues and narrows to 4.18-4.33 Ga under a different clock model.

authors: Weiss, Sousa, Mrnjavac, Neukirchen, Roettger, Nelson-Sathi, Martin
claim: 355 protein families (~0.1% of 286,514 clusters) trace to LUCA: anaerobic, CO2-fixing, H2-dependent, Wood-Ljungdahl, N2-fixing, thermophilic.
note: Correct. Full text not read: Green OA copy at zenodo.org/record/3451085 returns HTTP 410 Gone (record removed); publisher copy closed; not in Europe PMC.

claim: A consensus view of the proteome of LUCA.
note: Correct. Full text: Compares eight prior LUCA studies: no single study agrees even moderately with any other; the consensus covers at minimum protein synthesis, amino acid and nucleotide metabolism, and nucleotide-derived cofactors.

claim: Review: universal paralogs keep phylogenetic signal from before LUCA.
note: Full text: A perspective; only a small number of universal paralog families are known, and signal is blurred by gene loss, horizontal transfer (xenologs can look like paralogs) and long-branch attraction; different families give slightly different roots.

claim: The unfinished reconstructed nature of LUCA.
note: Full text: A review/perspective, not new data: methods give only partly overlapping LUCA protein sets (e.g. different ATP synthase subunits), and reverse gyrase phylogenies undercut a hyperthermophilic LUCA.

authors: Luque, Piaulet-Ghorayeb, Radica, Xue, Zhang, Bean, Samra, Steinrueck
claim: Joint NIRISS+NIRSpec+MIRI analysis of K2-18 b finds insufficient evidence for DMS or DMDS; ethane-like molecules fit as well; ~25 more MIRI transits needed for a 3-sigma test.
checked_against: full text (arxiv.org/pdf/2505.13407v1 (arXiv v1 of the A&A paper))
note: Correct. Full text: The ~25 transits (mean 26, SD 13 over 1,000 simulations) are for a 3-sigma rejection of a flat line assuming the best-fit DMS/DMDS model is true; only ~4 K2-18 b transits are observable by JWST per year.

claim: RNA-catalysed RNA polymerisation: accurate and general RNA-templated primer extension (class I polymerase).
note: Bartel lab; start of the polymerase lineage. Full text not read: Closed access (OpenAlex oa=closed); not in Europe PMC or PMC.

claim: Cross-replicating RNA ligases amplify exponentially without proteins, doubling time ~1 h.
note: Full text: Each ligase is made by joining two pre-made RNA oligonucleotide substrates (not mononucleotides) at 42 C; growth needs a continuous supply of those substrates; >10^8-fold over 30 h by serial transfer; heritable information limited to 2 loci with 12 alleles each.

claim: Ribozyme-catalysed transcription of an active ribozyme.
note: Full text not read: Closed access (OpenAlex oa=closed); not in Europe PMC or PMC.

note: Full text not read: Europe PMC copy exists (PMC5024611), but the fetch was stopped by an automated content-safety filter in the reading tool; not retried.

claim: Improved polymerase synthesises its ancestor, the class I ligase, as three strands, but few assembled ligases are active because of copying errors.
note: Full text: Fidelity is 96% per nucleotide on an easy template but only 83% (plus 1.7% insertions) on the hardest ligase fragment; the polymerase also made the complement of each strand.

claim: Ribozyme-catalysed RNA synthesis using triplet building blocks.
note: Full text: The triplet polymerase (a heterodimer) made its own catalytic subunit only in five segments that were then assembled, with pre-made primers/oligos covering ~25% of junctions; low efficiency, no full self-replication.
